questions.question: Curved denoising paths waste steps that bills count. What straightens the path?
options: More curved steps
Random path directions
No conditioning on progress
Time-conditioned velocity with rectified flows
questions.explanation: Straight paths need fewer steps. This lesson matches flows with time features.

questions.question: In train, what target velocity corresponds to x_t=t*x1+(1-t)*x0?
options: x0 + x1
x1 - x0
x_t / t for every t
A fresh Gaussian unrelated to x0 and x1
questions.explanation: The straight-line interpolation has constant derivative x1-x0, which train uses as the supervised target.

questions.question: What does `sample` do with num_steps=4?
options: It starts at t=0 and adds four forward-noise steps
It draws four independent final samples without evaluating the net
It uses dt=0.25 and takes four Euler updates while t moves from 1 toward 0
It changes the network's hidden width to four
questions.explanation: sample sets dt=1/num_steps, initializes x from Gaussian noise, and loops four times with t=1-i*dt and x-=dt*v.

questions.question: Why does forward include both t and t² along with sinusoidal time features?
options: They force every Euler step to use the same velocity
They make the data distribution two-dimensional instead of one-dimensional
They replace the need to sample x0 and x1
They provide the velocity network with several explicit representations of the continuous integration time
questions.explanation: The features encode the scalar time in polynomial and periodic forms so the MLP can condition its velocity prediction on t.

questions.question: What does train optimize with backward for each sampled interpolation?
options: The squared difference between the predicted velocity and x1-x0
The squared distance between x_t and zero regardless of time
A KL divergence between the two Gaussian endpoint distributions
The histogram count of samples greater than zero
questions.explanation: backward starts with d_out=2*(out-target), where target is the straight-line velocity x1-x0.

questions.question: Why does the demo compare 1-, 2-, 4-, 8-, and 20-step Euler samples?
options: It changes the training data mixture after the network is trained
It shows how numerical integration step count affects the quality and mode balance of generated samples
It tests five different codebooks for the same latent vector
It measures only the runtime of histogram rendering
questions.explanation: The same learned vector field is integrated with different discretizations, so the printed histograms and left/right counts expose the speed-quality trade-off.
